CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to evaluate the ongoing management of generalized anxiety disorder, insomnia, persistent fatigue, and tension-type headaches, with a focus on treatment efficacy and symptomatology changes since the last visit.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his follow-up appointment, bringing his symptom diary as previously instructed. He reports a continued stability in his generalized anxiety disorder, noting that the sertraline 300 mg daily remains effective. He describes a marked improvement in his ability to manage anxiety in social situations, attributing this success to his adherence to cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) and consistent medication use.
In terms of insomnia, Mr. Smith indicates that while the frequency of nocturnal awakenings has not significantly changed, he reports an improvement in the quality of sleep. He continues to utilize trazodone at 100 mg at bedtime, which he feels has contributed positively, although he still experiences some difficulty achieving restorative sleep. He expresses interest in exploring additional non-pharmacological interventions, such as guided relaxation techniques or sleep hygiene practices.
The tension-type headaches have remained stable, with an average occurrence of once weekly. He rates the intensity of his headaches at 3 out of 10, stating ibuprofen 600 mg provides satisfactory relief. However, he is eager to discuss potential preventive strategies, including the possibility of increasing his topiramate dosage or other therapeutic options.
Persistent fatigue continues to be a significant concern for Mr. Smith. He reports that while bupropion 150 mg daily helps to some extent, he still experiences episodes of cognitive fog and diminished energy levels, particularly during high-stress work periods. He expresses a desire to evaluate adjunctive treatments to ameliorate these symptoms.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 300 mg daily (continued) 2. Trazodone 100 mg at bedtime (continued) 3. Lisinopril 10 mg daily (continued) 4. Ibuprofen 600 mg as needed for headache relief (continued) 5. Topiramate 150 mg daily (continued) 6. Lorazepam 1 mg twice daily as needed (continued) 7. Melatonin 20 mg at bedtime (continued) 8. Modafinil 100 mg in the morning (continued) 9. Bupropion 150 mg daily (continued)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to engage in regular physical activity, including yoga and brisk walking, which he finds beneficial for managing stress and maintaining overall wellness. He reports a commitment to mindfulness practices, although work-related stress occasionally disrupts this routine. His active social life remains a vital component of his anxiety management, providing him with emotional support and engagement.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Anxiety levels stable; improved sleep quality; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms reported. - Neurological: Headache frequency stable; intensity rated as mild; no dizziness or visual disturbances noted. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Persistent fatigue continues; no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 122/76 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert, oriented; appears moderately fatigued but engaged; mood appears stable with mild anxiety. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed; no tenderness in the temporal region. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears stable with mild anxiety.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 300 mg daily. Maintain CBT sessions; reassess progress at the next visit. Lorazepam at 1 mg twice daily as needed for acute anxiety will remain on the regimen. 2. Insomnia: Continue trazodone at 100 mg at bedtime. Implement a sleep hygiene regimen including relaxation techniques and evaluate the effectiveness of these strategies at the next appointment. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue topiramate at 150 mg daily; maintain ibuprofen at 600 mg as needed. Consider increasing topiramate dosage to 200 mg daily if headache frequency does not improve. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Continue bupropion at 150 mg daily; encourage ongoing exercise and stress management techniques. Consider referral to a sleep specialist if fatigue persists and explore potential adjunctive medications if no improvement is observed.
Follow-up appointment is scheduled for 2029-11-01 to continue monitoring symptom progression, medication efficacy, and address any new concerns. Mr. Smith is encouraged to maintain a detailed log of his symptoms, medication responses, and any potential triggers for his anxiety or headaches to facilitate ongoing management.
